verdict.rationale: Marqeta's own velocity controls and authorization controls are configurable rules that the platform enforces automatically at transaction time, limiting spend amount, frequency and merchants. That is a narrow, spend-specific form of event-triggered rules. Webhooks and JIT funding only notify or delegate decisions to the customer's own system, so they are building blocks rather than a rules engine and earn no credit here. Missing for 10: a general rule engine that maps arbitrary events to configurable actions, documentation of any action beyond restricting or declining spend (e.g., auto card-state transitions on events), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: You can configure velocity controls to limit how much users can spend and the number of transactions they can make in a given span of time.
If multiple velocity controls apply to the same user, the user cannot exceed any of the defined spending limits.
An authorization control limits spending by specified users at specified merchants.
Spend controls: Set customizable velocity limits, spending caps, and merchant restrictions.
